title: ALMA Detection of Extreme Blueshifted Ionized Gas within 0.2 pc of Sgr A* from -480 to -300 km s<SUP>-1</SUP>
question: Is there extreme high-velocity blue-shifted ionized gas within the inner parsec of Sgr A*, and does it indicate a jet or wind-driven outflow?

data.sensitivity: H30a cube sigma = 0.4 mJy per channel at 3 km/s; continuum ~0.8 mJy/beam (Jul 12/13), ~1.6 (Jul 18/19)

what.value: Proper motion transverse velocities of K25 (865 km/s), K33 (313 km/s), K32 (656), K41 (215)

evidence.quote: consider the K25 and K33 sources (cite: zhao09), which are 0$.\!\!^{\prime\prime}$52 and 0$.\!\!^{\prime\prime}$41 away from C1

what.value: Radio recombination line relation for line intensity vs EM

evidence.quote: The line intensity at 231.9 GHz can be expressed as (cite: wilson12):

recipe.goal: Self-calibrate and image continuum and H30a cube
recipe.method: Combine spws, phase self-cal three times then amp+phase, apply to cube after uv linear continuum subtraction; Briggs 0.5

recipe.goal: Locate and characterize high-velocity components C1-C4
recipe.method: Elliptical Gaussian fits to integrated intensity in narrow velocity ranges; multi-Gaussian spectral fits; PV diagrams
EM from line intensity with Te = 7.5e3-12.5e3 K, path length = source size; density lower limit; total mass of region
assumptions: Te 7.5-12.5e3 K (1e4 K for total mass); path length equal to source size

recipe.method: Escape velocity for 4e6 Msun BH combined with literature proper motions; momentum deposition rate for jet (gamma~2.7) or wind (1250 km/s) outflow
assumptions: Central mass 4e6 Msun, distance 8.5 kpc, flat mass profile

evidence.quote: an average electron density of 1.6$\times 10^4$ cm$^{-3}$ and total mass of 0.052 M$_{\odot}$
a mass outflow rate of $1.8\times10^{-7}$ M$_{\odot}$ year$^{-1}$ would satisfy a jet origin
the required mass-loss rate is $4\times10^{-5}$ M$_{\odot}$  yr$^{-1}$
the escape velocity at a *projected* distance of 0.09 pc (2$.\!\!^{\prime\prime}$2) is then $\sim$ 620 km s$^{-1}$

not_stated_but_needed: Self-calibration solution intervals and reference antenna
Cell size, image size, deconvolver, masking and clean threshold
How the coordinate shift of +61/-123 mas was derived and which reference dataset
Gaussian fitting details and the line-fit procedure
Origin of the 'size' deconvolution choice and uncertainties on measured values
score_reason: Public data and key weighting and version given, but many imaging and self-cal details missing and no uncertainties.
rediscovery_reason: Public data, main results (velocities, densities) are numeric, and the recipe is mostly stated, though details are missing.
